title: Synthetic failure injector and auto-repair playbook for prompt-set regressions
author: Jordan Kim
release_notes: Adds a synthetic failure injector for targeted prompt-set regressions, an automated degradation scorer, and an operational playbook that can run as a CI hook or offline repair job. Improves regression triage and reduces mean time to rollback for model+prompt regressions.
description: Motivation: Prompt-set regressions are often intermittent and hard to reproduce in CI because the failure signal is sparse. This PR adds a deterministic, configurable synthetic-failure injector that can (1) emulate degradations across cohorts and token-level behaviors, (2) run in CI or as a scheduled job to validate prompt-set quality gates, and (3) pair with an auto-repair playbook that suggests targeted prompt holdouts and lightweight rollback patches. Summary of changes: new injector library, a degradation scorer that aggregates semantic + metric deltas, an orchestrator hook to run controlled backfills, integration tests and a human-readable playbook in docs. The description below includes a short checklist, commits and high-level rollout notes. Checklist: - [x] Library implementation (eval_harness/probes/synthetic_injector.py) - [x] Degradation scorer and threshold config - [x] CI hook and k8s job manifest - [x] Integration tests and examples - [x] Playbook and runbook docs - [x] Backwards-compatible defaults (disabled by default in public CI) Commits (summary): - Add synthetic injector core and configuration parsing (seeded RNG, cohort selectors, perturbation profiles) - Add degradation_scorer with semantic embedding delta + token-level metrics - Add replay_manager hooks to orchestrate injected runs and capture traces - Add CI hook definition and k8s job manifest to run small holdout backfills - Add examples/holdout prompt_set and integration tests - Add docs/playbook and example commands - Fixes from review: improved logging and deterministic seeding How to use: The CI hook can be enabled per-prompt-set via eval config; by default it runs a small, bounded backfill of 200 examples against a mirrored canary model. Operators can tune profiles to simulate hallucination, truncation, and latency-induced token drops. The auto-repair playbook produces a short, actionable runbook: holdout suggested prompts, candidate patch (prompt edits or model pin), risk score, and rollback steps for Redwood Console. Testing: unit coverage for injector utilities, integration test runs on the example prompt set, and staged smoke on staging CI before enabling on main. Rollout plan: enable as opt-in on staging for two weeks, collect degradation metrics, then flip opt-in for a set of critical prompt-sets before enabling strict CI gating. Related work: ENG-5423 (regression triage), PM-1280 (quality gating roadmap).
